svg.font-family: IBM Plex Sans, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
svg.aria-label: The seven steps of the procedure. Each step has what goes in on the left and what comes out on the right. The output of one step flows down into the next. Step three has two outcomes. When the changed step gives the same output, the case goes straight to the label table. When it differs, the case goes to the model calls of step four.
svg.text: (b) The seven steps, with what goes in and what comes out of each

g.text: 1 Split the patch into single changes
compare the two programs statement by statement
a change in a step with no probe is marked as not watchable
the program before and after the patch
the line numbers of each change
which steps have a probe
the list of single changes, each with its step
every subset of changes that still runs as a program
the changes we cannot watch
2 Run both programs and record every step
the buggy and the patched program, every test question
the order in which steps ran gives the graph
the test questions and their expected answers
probes at the eight steps
the same model, packages and data for every run
what passed through each probe, per run and question
the order of steps, with the tool branch and the memory loop
which changes actually ran in each run

svg.text: the recorded states and the graph

g.text: 3 Rerun only the changed step and compare
feed the recorded input of that step to its changed code
same output, the recorded result stands
different output, rerun the code after it, call the model for new prompts
the recorded input and output of that step
the changed code of that step
recorded model answers, filed by the prompt that made them
no difference on this question, result as recorded
no model call needed for this change and question
a changed output, the rest of the run is rerun
still open where the model needs a new call

svg.text: settled cases go straight to the label table

g.text: 4 Call the model where still needed, one call at a time
the next call goes to the comparison that is least settled
stop when it is settled or the budget is spent
the open comparisons and how sure we are of each
the confidence level, the margin and the budget
a change that cannot alter behaviour, as a control
new model answers, for new prompts only
passes out of runs, per question and per side
the control's passes

svg.text: pass or fail at the step and at the end, per run

g.text: 5 Score each intermediate check
does a pass here predict a pass at the end
does it catch the bug, and did the checked step run
the intermediate check result of every run
the final check result of every run
runs with one change taken out
how often a pass here means a pass at the end
how many removed changes the check catches
how often the checked step actually ran

svg.text: the pass counts and the settled cases

g.text: 6 Write the label table
one row per pair of versions that differ by one change
pairs that cannot be compared fairly are left out
passes per side, and the settled cases
which changes ran, and how often
the confidence level and the margin
pass rate of each side, with its interval
the effect of the change, and its effect when it ran
the label, required, removable or not decided
7 Find the smallest sets of changes that fix the case
two changes are independent when the first does not alter what reaches the second
prefer fewer steps touched, then fewer changes
the label table
the graph of steps
the pass level a fix must reach
every set of changes that fixes the case, smallest marked
the alternative repairs
the chosen repair

svg.text: Steps 1, 2 and 5, and step 3 on code, need no model call. The model is called only in steps 3 and 4, and only for a prompt the records have not seen.
